samples.question: The picture is a cream board littered with small decorative squares that mean nothing. Lying on the board are several large SQUARE TILES, all of exactly the same size and all far bigger than any decorative square. Exactly six of these large tiles are joined edge to edge, with no gap between them, into one single connected piece: that piece is the NET. Every other large tile is a LOOSE TILE: it stands clear of the net and clear of every other loose tile, with visible cream board all round it, and loose tiles mean nothing. The six squares of the net all have different colours, one each of red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple, and exactly one of them carries a white DOT at its centre; loose tiles and decorative squares may repeat any of those colours and never carry a dot. Fold the net along the shared edges of its six squares so that it closes up into a cube, each square becoming one face of that cube. In the folded cube the dotted face lies directly opposite exactly one other face, the face it never touches: that face is the OPPOSITE FACE. Its colour is the answer. Every scene is sampled so that cheap reading fails: the opposite face is never a square that touches the dotted square along an edge on the board, no square of the net lies two straight steps away from the dotted square along a row or a column, the dotted square touches at most two other squares of the net, and the opposite face is never the single square lying farthest from the dotted square in board steps. Tile size, tile count, the six net colours and the total amount of ink are the same whatever the answer is, and the net can sit anywhere on the board, so no colour, position, size, count or amount of ink identifies the answer on its own. Fold the net into a cube and find the face opposite the dotted face. What is its colour? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.
